question: A 21-year-old man presents to the emergency room requesting surgery to remove "microchips," which he believes were implanted in his brain by "Russian spies" 6 months ago to control his thoughts. He also reports hearing the "spies" talk to each other through embedded "microspeakers." You notice that his hair appears unwashed and some of his clothes are on backward. Urine toxicology is negative for illicit drugs. Which of the following additional findings are you most likely to see in this patient during the course of his illness?

options.opa: Amnesia, multiple personality states, and de-realization
options.opd: Grandiose delusions, racing thoughts, and pressured speech
options.ope: Intrusive thoughts, ritualized behaviors, and anxious mood

analysis: The patient is exhibiting symptoms consistent with a psychotic disorder, likely schizophrenia. The presence of delusions (belief in implanted microchips by Russian spies) and auditory hallucinations (hearing spies talk through microspeakers) are key features. The disheveled appearance and disorganized behavior (clothes on backward) are indicative of impaired self-care and possible cognitive deficits. The most likely additional findings in this patient during the course of his illness would be asociality (withdrawal from social interactions), flat affect (lack of emotional expression), and alogia (poverty of speech). These negative symptoms are commonly seen in schizophrenia.
